item.title: NDC names Ibezi, Umeh, Nwoye to Anambra campaign council
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has appointed former member of the House of Representatives, Hon. Ifeanyi Ibezi, as coordinator of its Anambra State campaign council ahead of the 2027 general elections. The campaign council also features Senator Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central; Senator Tony Nwoye, representing Anambra North; and Chief Ebuka Onunkwo, the party’s senatorial candidate for Anambra South. Other members include Emeka Kissinger Osisi as State Director of Youth Mobilisation, Barr. Ogechukwu Ekweozor as Director of Women Mobilisation, DIG Celestine Okoye (rtd) as Director of Security and AIG Innocent Ndubueze Anene (rtd) as Director of Election Monitoring and Vote Protection. The appointments were announced in a statement signed by the party’s State Director of Media and Publicity, Dr. Tony Onyima. The statement also named Chief Egwuoba Okika Innocent as Deputy State Coordinator, former Speaker of the Anambra State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Ikem Uzoezie, as State Chairman, and Barr. Paulinus Akabogu Izuchukwu as State Campaign Secretary. Campaign coordinators for the three senatorial districts are Hon. Kingsley Nwafor for Anambra South, Hon. Chuka Ezenwunne for Anambra Central and Hon. Chigbo Enwezor for Anambra North. All serving federal and state lawmakers elected on the party’s platform are also members of the campaign council. The council will operate through various directorates covering media and publicity, finance, logistics, women and youth mobilisation, security, grassroots mobilisation, election monitoring and vote protection, new media, protocol, policy research and documentation, and special duties. Onyima will serve as State Director of Media and Publicity, with Paschal Azubuike as his deputy, while Hon. Lady Azuka Enemuo and Mrs. Chika Ezeali will oversee finance as director and deputy director, respectively. The council also has coordinators for the 21 local government areas of the state as part of efforts to extend the party’s campaign activities to the grassroots. The NDC Anambra State Campaign Council is scheduled to be inaugurated on Wednesday, November 4, in Awka. item.title: Soludo confirms Peter Obi’s wife as child’s godmother
item.description: Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has confirmed that the wife of former governor Peter Obi is the godmother of one of his children, months after a public disagreement over the relationship between their families. Soludo also disclosed that his wife, Nonye, is the confirmation godmother of Obi’s daughter, clarifying the family relationship that became a subject of public discussion in September. The governor made the disclosure in an interview with BBC News Igbo on Monday, describing Obi as a close friend and insisting that their families remained on good terms despite their political differences. “Peter Obi and I are good friends. Our two families are on good terms. His wife was the godmother of my child at baptism, and my wife was the godmother of his child at confirmation,” he said. Soludo explained that their differences were political, particularly over their preferences for who should govern Anambra State. He said he did not hold Obi’s political position against him, despite their disagreement over the state’s leadership. “I have a different vision of who should be governor of Anambra State. I am contesting, and he supported whoever he felt should be governor. I prevailed by the grace of God, and I don’t hold it against him,” the governor said. item.title: Utomi faults APC over alleged extravagance amid hardship
item.description: Political economist, Prof. Pat Utomi, has criticised the All Progressives Congress (APC) administration over what he described as extravagant lifestyles among public officials amid economic hardship in the country. Utomi said it was contradictory for government officials to describe Nigeria as poor while allegedly displaying luxury vehicles, including Maybachs, G-Wagons and Rolls-Royces, and travelling in private jets. He made the remarks in a post on his X account on Tuesday, arguing that the lifestyles of public office holders should reflect the economic realities confronting ordinary Nigerians. “You cannot stand before the world and declare that Nigeria is poor, then turn around and parade your ministers in million-dollar Maybachs, G-Wagons and Rolls-Royces, while public officials fly around in private jets. Your optics contradict your narrative, your lifestyle contradicts your statistics,” he said. The former presidential candidate said if Nigeria was indeed poor, government spending and the management of public resources should reflect the country’s economic circumstances. He argued that members of the executive and legislature should demonstrate fiscal restraint, particularly when citizens were being asked to endure economic difficulties. According to him, public office should not be treated as a licence for extravagance, adding that government officials had a responsibility to show restraint in the use of public resources. “The APC needs to understand that public office is not a licence for extravagance. If citizens must endure economic hardship, those entrusted with their taxes must also demonstrate restraint,” Utomi said. He added that displaying luxury lifestyles while asking Nigerians to endure economic hardship could deepen public resentment and reinforce perceptions that government officials were insensitive to the plight of ordinary citizens. item.title: Atiku faults Cross River security over alleged estate robberies
item.description: The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has criticised the security arrangements around Cross River State Governor’s private residence in Calabar, following reports of alleged robberies in neighbouring homes. Atiku said residents of the estate where Governor Bassey Otu’s private residence is located had complained of repeated burglaries despite the presence of armed policemen and two roadblocks securing the governor’s property. According to him, one resident reportedly lost an air conditioner and a freezer to burglars, while another disclosed that two houses on a nearby street were attacked last week. The former Vice President disclosed this in a post on his X account on Tuesday, questioning the disparity between the security provided for the governor and the protection available to residents living in the same neighbourhood. He said the governor had been operating from his private residence for nearly three years while the Government House was undergoing renovation, yet residents living nearby remained exposed to security threats. “This is security, APC style: two roadblocks for the governor, and none for the people next door,” Atiku said. He questioned the capacity of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to address insecurity across the state, asking what it could offer communities outside the state capital if residents living beside the governor could not sleep without fear. Atiku also outlined his proposed security reforms, pledging to transform the Nigeria Police Force from what he described as a regime-protecting force into a citizen-focused public service. He said his administration would expand police personnel towards the international benchmark of one officer to every 450 citizens to improve security coverage across communities. The ADC presidential candidate also promised to establish community-based security and intelligence networks to enable neighbourhoods to identify and report threats before criminal activities occur. “Security that stops at the governor’s gate is not security; it is a fence,” he added. item.title: US Strikes Iran’s Qeshm Island — Report
item.description: The United States on Monday attacked Iran’s Qeshm Island, the Wall Street Journal reported, even as President Donald Trump signaled progress in negotiations with Tehran to end the eight-month-old conflict. The Journal, citing unnamed US officials, described the strike against Qeshm, the largest island in the Strait of Hormuz, as the latest of a series of limited strikes Washington has secretly carried out against Iran in recent weeks. Iranian state news agency IRNA reported five explosions in rapid succession were heard on the island, and that some residents reported seeing two aircraft flying in its skies. The Pentagon referred questions about the reported strikes to US Central Command, which did not immediately respond to an AFP request for comment late Monday. The Journal reported that the US has been engaged in smaller-scale strikes against Iran for several weeks. It said some officials described the assaults as defensive in nature to prevent Iran from having the freedom to attack commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz, a key conduit for oil shipments that has been largely blocked since the war began in late February. The paper said the US has not publicly announced the attacks, so as not to signal any intention of resuming major combat operations. item.title: NIMC arrests illegal NIN operators, seizes enrolment equipment
item.description: By Emmanuel Elebeke The National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) has intensified its crackdown on illegal National Identification Number (NIN) enrolment, unauthorised data modification and extortion, following an enforcement operation that led to several arrests in Gwagwalada and other locations. The Commission disclosed this in a statement, saying its Inspectorate Compliance and Enforcement Unit (ICEU) carried out the operation and seized equipment allegedly used for illegal enrolment activities. It said the exercise was part of efforts to curb unauthorised enrolment and unethical practices while protecting the integrity, security and credibility of Nigeria’s National Identity Management System. NIMC noted that many of the challenges encountered by NIN holders resulted from attempts to bypass official enrolment procedures. It stressed that NIN enrolment could only be conducted at its approved centres, while requests for modification of personal data could be processed through its self-service modification platform. The Commission also advised NIN holders to download the NINAuth application from the iOS App Store or Google Play Store to access security features, print their NIN slips and enjoy other related services. The Director-General and Chief Executive Officer of NIMC, Engr. Abisoye Coker-Odusote, reiterated the Commission’s zero tolerance for extortion and unethical practices. She said the Commission remained committed to providing seamless and hitch-free NIN enrolment services for Nigerians and legal residents. NIMC urged applicants and existing NIN holders to use only its approved channels for enrolment and other related services. It advised members of the public to visit www.nimc.gov.ng or follow its verified social media platforms for accurate information. item.title: WAFCON Victory: Tinubu Fulfils $100,000 Promise To Super Falcons
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has fulfilled his $100,000 promise to the Super Falcons, following their historic victory at the 2025 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON), where Nigeria clinched a record-extending 10th continental title. ‎According to the National Sports Commission, the players have begun receiving payments of about ₦140 million, representing the naira equivalent of the $100,000 reward promised by the President after the team staged a remarkable comeback to defeat hosts Morocco in the final in July 2025. ‎The Super Falcons, who were trailing 2-0, produced a spirited second-half performance to stun the hosts and reclaim the African crown, further cementing their status as the continent’s most successful women’s national team. Super Falcons celebrate a goal at the WAFCON ‎Team captain, Rasheedat Ajibade, expressed gratitude to the President for fulfilling his promise, describing the gesture as a welcome recognition of the team’s achievement and contribution to Nigerian sports. ‎The payment is another demonstration of President Tinubu’s commitment to rewarding sporting excellence and motivating Nigerian athletes to achieve greater success on the international stage. The Super Falcons warming up ahead of a game. Photo credit: cafonline.com ‎The President had similarly promised and delivered $100,000 rewards to members of D’Tigress following their triumph at the 2025 FIBA Women’s AfroBasket, where Nigeria secured a fifth consecutive continental title. ‎The Commission commended President Tinubu for his consistent support for Nigerian athletes and for demonstrating that sporting excellence deserves tangible recognition. ‎The Commission added that the President’s commitment has strengthened confidence among athletes and sports administrators while encouraging a culture of reward, accountability and national pride. item.title: AI not enemy of democracy — Amupitan
item.description: THE Chairman of Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan, has defended the use of Artificial Intelligence in election management. According to him, the technology is not a threat to democracy, despite its potential misuse by malicious actors. Amupitan said AI could improve electoral administration through efficient voter registration, logistics planning, data analysis and the management of large voter databases. He warned that advances in generative AI had made it easier to create deceptive content capable of undermining public confidence in elections. The INEC chairman, who stated these at The Beyond the Ballot Summit in Abuja yesterday, explained that electoral management bodies worldwide had adopted AI-assisted processes to improve administrative efficiency and strengthen election planning. The INEC chairman’s remarks came amid preparations for the 2027 general election, with the commission recently announcing plans to integrate AI into Nigeria’s electoral system. item.title: Nigeria needs leaders equipped for changing realities — Sam Adeyemi
item.description: By Ogochukwu Agha LAGOS—THE Senior Pastor of Daystar Christian Centre, Pastor Sam Adeyemi, yesterday, warned that Nigeria cannot afford leaders who learn on the job, lamenting that many occupying positions of authority have never received formal leadership training, despite the country’s mounting economic and social challenges. Adeyemi spoke in Lagos ahead of the 2026 edition of the church’s annual Excellence in Leadership Conference (ELC), scheduled for November 5 and 6, 2026, at the Daystar Christian Centre, Oregun in Lagos. Making a case for deliberate leadership development, he said: “Sometimes only God knows who is going to be governor. Who knows who is going to be senator tomorrow? And most people occupying leadership positions in our country have not learned leadership anywhere.” He urged Nigerians to take advantage of the conference, themed ‘Leading in Uncertainty’, describing participation as “a great investment in their lives. In a joint message, Adeyemi and his wife, Nike Adeyemi, who co-host the conference, said the event would explore “what it truly means to lead when the ground keeps shifting economically, socially, and personally. “Previous participants have described the conference as a game-changer, with some attributing practical improvements in their careers and businesses to lessons acquired at the event”, the statement reads. They explained that the theme was informed by prevailing realities, including volatile markets, rising living costs, policy changes and transformations in the world of work, against the backdrop of an approaching general election cycle. “Participants would be equipped to stand firm, think clearly, and lead boldly, while learning how to turn uncertainty into a leadership advantage,” they added. Adeyemi spoke in Lagos ahead of the 2026 edition of the church’s annual Excellence in Leadership Conference (ELC), scheduled for November 5 and 6, 2026, at the Daystar Christian Centre, Oregun in Lagos. Making a case for deliberate leadership development, he said: “Sometimes only God knows who is going to be governor. Who knows who is going to be senator tomorrow? And most people occupying leadership positions in our country have not learned leadership anywhere.” He urged Nigerians to take advantage of the conference, themed ‘Leading in Uncertainty’, describing participation as “a great investment in their lives. In a joint message, Adeyemi and his wife, Nike Adeyemi, who co-host the conference, said the event would explore “what it truly means to lead when the ground keeps shifting economically, socially, and personally. “Previous participants have described the conference as a game-changer, with some attributing practical improvements in their careers and businesses to lessons acquired at the event”, the statement reads. They explained that the theme was informed by prevailing realities, including volatile markets, rising living costs, policy changes and transformations in the world of work, against the backdrop of an approaching general election cycle. “Participants would be equipped to stand firm, think clearly, and lead boldly, while learning how to turn uncertainty into a leadership advantage,” they added. Police confirm attack on officers The spokesperson of the Zone 10 Police Command headquarters in Sokoto, ASP Abdallah Faruk Ambursa, confirmed the attack. The zone covers Kebbi, Sokoto, and Zamfara states. He said the victims were officers attached to the headquarters and were travelling for official duty. He said he could not provide further details because the incident occurred in Zamfara State, where the state police command was investigating the matter. “I cannot give details of the development or the identities of the victims for now until after the investigation,” he said. Ambursa, however, disclosed that the victims were evacuated to Sokoto but declined to disclose where their bodies were deposited. He further said those injured in the attack were receiving treatment at a hospital. When asked about the number of officers involved, Ambursa said the Zamfara Police Command would give a detailed report subsequently. “We await a detailed report. The data was compiled from news reports confirmed by police authorities. The deaths involved attacks by bandits, gunmen and terrorists, as well as road accidents and shootings by fellow police officers. Yobe State recorded the highest number of casualties, with 17 officers killed, followed by Zamfara and Kebbi states with 14 each. Katsina recorded five deaths, while Borno and Taraba recorded four each. Rivers, Sokoto, Plateau, Enugu, Lagos and Imo recorded three deaths each. A breakdown of the figures showed that bandits were responsible for 35 deaths, gunmen 29 and Boko Haram terrorists 22. Two officers were killed by Lakurawa terrorists. Other deaths included three officers shot by fellow policemen, four killed in road incidents involving accidents and hit-and-run drivers, one killed by kidnappers, one by hoodlums and another by thugs. Some of the deadliest attacks occurred in Kebbi State, where 10 policemen were killed in a gun duel with bandits at Rafin Makuku axis of Sakaba Local Government Area on August 10. Police authorities said the incident occurred at about 9:25 a.m. on Monday, August 10, 2026, when police operatives intercepted the suspected bandits who were moving between Zamfara and Kebbi states. The police said 17 suspected bandits were neutralised during the encounter, while four motorcycles belonging to the attackers were destroyed. In Yobe, 17 officers were reportedly killed during an attack on the Nigerian Army Special Forces School in Buni Yadi on May 16. “The officers, who were undergoing specialised operational training at the institution, lost their lives when the militants launched a coordinated ‌attack on the facility from multiple directions,” then police spokesman, DCP Anthony Okon Placid, said in a statement. He said several soldiers were also killed, though he did not give a figure for military casualties. The command identified the slain officers as Paul Ina, Mohammed Yusuf, Oge Ikechukwu and Edeh Andrew. Their bodies were recovered from surrounding bushes during search and rescue operations, the police said. Seven civilians were also killed. Their bodies were recovered after the attack and deposited at a mortuary, according to the command. In January, Inspector Sani Malumfashi was allegedly shot dead by a fellow officer at Intels, Onne in Rivers State. In October, Corporal Amos Yusuf reportedly shot his colleague, Corporal Grace Onimisi, dead at their residence in Asco Camp, Ajaokuta, Kogi State, before taking his own life. item.title: Tinubu to unveil book on Olanipekun’s landmark cases
item.description: By Henry Ojelu LAGOS—PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu will on November 19 unveil a six-volume publication documenting landmark cases handled by renowned legal practitioner, Chief Wole Olanipekun, SAN, over his 50 years in the Nigerian legal profession. The publication, titled ‘Wole Olanipekun through the cases’, examines Olanipekun’s contributions to the development of Nigerian law and jurisprudence through commentaries on significant cases he handled during his five decades at the Bar. The unveiling will take place at the WOC Justice Summit, an initiative of Wole Olanipekun & Co, which brings together stakeholders to deliberate on issues affecting the justice sector. The event will take place 24 hours after Olanipekun’s 75th birthday, having been born on November 18, 1951. The six-volume publication features forewords by the Chief Justice of Nigeria, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, and the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN. It brings together contributions from retired judicial officers, academics, Senior Advocates of Nigeria and other prominent legal practitioners, offering an examination of the breadth of Olanipekun’s legal practice. and his influence on the country’s jurisprudence. The legal luminary is currently Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of the Governing Council of the University of Lagos, having previously held similar positions at the University of Ibadan and Ajayi Crowther University. He is also Chairman of the Board of Trustees of Ajayi Crowther University and Chancellor of Bamidele Olumilua University of Education, Science and Technology, Ikere-Ekiti. item.description: *Residents accuse developer of canal encroachment, harassment By Godwin Oritse LAGOS—IN a dramatic development that has raised concerns over compliance with planning regulations in Lagos State, the Deputy Governor, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, was reportedly locked out of a disputed construction site at Osborne Foreshore Phase II Estate, Ikoyi, on Saturday by Kenshad International Ltd, a developer facing allegations of planning violations and environmental infractions from residents. Hamzat, accompanied by a high-powered delegation of government officials and political leaders, waited for more than 30 minutes at the entrance of the development named Abba Court on Mahogany Close, but the gates were shut. The incident occurred during a visit prompted by complaints from residents, who accused the developer of engaging in unauthorised activities they said could threaten the safety and environmental integrity of the estate. “Why did he refuse to allow the Deputy Governor and his team in if he has nothing to hide?” a resident asked, expressing suspicion over the incident. The Deputy Governor expressed displeasure over the developer’s conduct and assured residents that the Lagos State Government would investigate the complaints. At a meeting with Hamzat tagged ‘Osborne Phase II residents and public leaders’ dialogue,’ residents accused the developer of constructing beneath high-tension electricity lines, constructing slabs over a canal, and carrying out sand-filling activities that have narrowed the water outlets in the estate. Speaking on behalf of the residents, Mr. Adebisi Taiwo alleged that the developer created an unauthorised back gate through which thugs were brought into the estate to intimidate those who questioned its activities. Taiwo also accused the developer of using security agents and unscrupulous officials to harass and intimidate them. item.title: PAMA backs FG’s commitment to affordable long-term industrial financing
item.description: By Yinka Kolawole The Pan African Manufacturers Association (PAMA) has welcomed the Federal Government’s commitments to improve energy supply, provide affordable long-term financing for industries, strengthen local procurement, secure industrial corridors and establish quarterly engagements with manufacturers. According to the association, these priorities align with its broader commitment to advancing industrialisation, strengthening regional value chains and expanding intra-African trade. However, it stressed that effective implementation of the commitments would be critical to improving the operating environment for manufacturers, boosting industrial productivity and strengthening Nigeria’s competitiveness in regional and global markets. PAMA stated this while commending the Manufacturers Association of Nigeria (MAN) for the successful hosting of its 54th Annual General Meeting (AGM). Held under the theme, “Leveraging National Industrial Policy to Position Nigeria as Africa’s Industrial Hub,” the AGM focused on implementing the Nigeria Industrial Policy 2025 (NIP 2025), enhancing manufacturing competitiveness, expanding access to industrial finance, reducing energy costs and promoting local value addition. A major highlight of the event was the 6th Adeola Odutola Lecture, delivered by Dr. Kandeh Kolleh Yumkella, former Director-General of the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO). Discussions at the meeting emphasised the need to translate industrial policy commitments into tangible economic outcomes through effective implementation, institutional accountability and sustained collaboration between the public and private sectors. PAMA reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening partnership with MAN, noting that closer collaboration among manufacturers across Africa is essential to developing regional value chains, and expanding industrial capacity. and unlocking opportunities under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). It further emphasised the importance of building a competitive and integrated African manufacturing sector capable of driving sustainable economic growth, creating jobs and increasing the continent’s participation in regional and global trade. item.title: Procurement knowledge gap shuts small businesses out of FG contracts — Minister
item.description: By Yinka Kolawole Many small businesses in Nigeria are missing out on Federal Government contracts due to inadequate knowledge of public procurement procedures, Minister of State for Industry, Senator John Enoh, has said. Enoh stated this in Abuja at the launch of the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) Public Procurement Training Programme and digital learning portal organised by the Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP), adding that limited knowledge, weak internal processes and inadequate capacity were hindering small businesses from competing effectively for government contracts. He said many entrepreneurs lacked the skills to register, meet compliance requirements, interpret procurement documents, prepare competitive bids and execute government contracts. “Many businesses are excluded because of capacity constraints, limited knowledge, weak internal processes and insufficient capability,” the minister said. Enoh added that some businesses were disqualified because of missing documents, while the complexity of procurement procedures further restricted their participation. He said the knowledge gap increased the cost of doing business and deepened small businesses’ dependence on intermediaries, stressing the need to give women-owned enterprises and other small businesses equal opportunities to compete. The minister urged business associations to publicise procurement opportunities and educate their members on bidding requirements. He also called on ministries, departments and agencies (MDAs) to simplify procurement procedures, improve transparency and strengthen support for small businesses. Director-General of BPP, Adebowale Adedokun, said MSMEs account for about 96 per cent of businesses in Nigeria and contribute approximately 50 per cent of the nation’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP). He said despite their economic importance, many face barriers to public procurement, including inadequate technical knowledge and difficulties navigating bidding requirements, adding that the digital learning portal would provide free training tailored to Nigeria’s procurement system. item.title: AAUA bans signing-out ceremonies over security concerns
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The management of Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko (AAUA), Ondo State, has banned signing-out ceremonies and all related celebrations on campus over security concerns. The directive was contained in a circular issued by the Registrar, Dr Grace Olubunmi Babalola, dated October 30, 2026. According to the circular, the Vice-Chancellor, acting on behalf of the Senate, approved the ban in the interest of protecting lives and property within the university community. The management directed that no signing-out party, gathering, procession or other celebratory activity associated with the completion of academic programmes should be organised or held anywhere on campus until further notice. The directive takes immediate effect, with all students, particularly final-year students, urged to comply strictly. Deans, Heads of Departments, Heads of Units, security personnel and other relevant university officials have been directed to ensure strict enforcement and report any violation to the appropriate authorities. Babalola warned that students and other members of the university community who flout the directive would face disciplinary action in accordance with the institution’s extant laws and regulations. She added that cases involving suspected criminal conduct would be referred to law enforcement agencies for appropriate action. The Registrar urged members of the university community to cooperate with the management in maintaining a safe, peaceful and orderly campus environment, stressing that the suspension would remain in force until further notice.
